title: Super Mario World

masks.why: the status bar and the title's wooden frame are BG3 drawn in front (BGMODE $09) and laid out for 256 columns

issues: Enemies and coins appear 16-32 pixels past the SNES edge: the game creates its objects as they come near the SNES picture, so in the side columns they pop in.
At the start of a level the left side is empty: the level begins at the SNES picture's left edge.
Levels whose water or clouds are BG3 drawn in front (the layer-3 tides) lose that layer in the side columns.
No flicker: in the 4,000 frames checked the game never drew more sprites on a line than a SNES shows, so it changed nothing; it changes only lines over the limits.

Fast CPU switched on while the game starts hangs it on a black screen: the 65816 reaches the next step of its sound-driver handshake (writing $FF to $2141) about 8 ms after starting the driver instead of 31 ms, while the driver is still setting up and clears its input ports, so both wait for each other forever. A real 10.74 MHz 65816 would do the same. Traced: the 31 ms are the game clearing its work RAM ($00:8A4E, 8 KB) between the two steps, with no sound-port access, so the console's sound-port guard cannot keep it at SNES time. Switched on after the title appears, the game ran the 4,000 frames checked.

verified.how: Workshop --wms-test (E6), 4,000 frames of a pad script (title, new game, Yoshi's Island 2) in lockstep with the SNES console: widescreen's centre 256 columns identical to the SNES picture every frame, STAT77 and the sound identical, switched off frame-identical; no flicker changes only lines over the SNES's limits; better sound changes only the sound.
